title: Mitigate One, Skew Another? Tackling Intersectional Biases in Text-to-Image Models

bias_targets.methodology: Generating images with text-to-image models using occupational prompts and counterfactuals, then using a Visual Question Answering (VQA) model to classify the perceived gender (male, female) and measuring distribution skews via Wasserstein distance.

Generating images with text-to-image models using occupational prompts and counterfactuals, then using a VQA model to classify the perceived age group (young, middle-aged, old) and calculating distribution differences.

Generating images with text-to-image models using occupational prompts and counterfactuals, then using a VQA model to classify the perceived ethnicity (white, black, asian, south asian, middle eastern, hispanic) to measure distribution skews.
Generating images using occupational prompts and counterfactuals, followed by VQA classification of the generated person's body type (fat, slim, muscular) to analyze representational diversity.
Generating images using occupational prompts and VQA classification to determine the environmental setting (indoor, outdoor) associated with different subjects.
Using a VQA model to classify the attire (formal, informal) of subjects generated from text-to-image models prompted with various occupations and counterfactuals.
Using a VQA model to extract the perceived emotion (happy, sad, serious, tired) of subjects in images generated from occupational prompts to evaluate stereotypes in expressions.
Generating images with occupational prompts and using a VQA model to identify the presence of visible disability indicators (blindness/white cane, hearing aids, wheelchairs).
